extrapolated_salsa2.name: linear in n
extrapolated_salsa2.note: Slowest growth. Assumes each extra dimension costs a constant number of samples, which no learning-theoretic argument supports.

extrapolated_salsa2.name: exponential in n
extrapolated_salsa2.note: Constant multiplicative cost per added dimension.

extrapolated_salsa2.name: exponential in log2(secret-space size)
extrapolated_salsa2.note: The only model that sees the h increase from 2 to 3. Treats the cost as driven by how many secrets must be distinguished.

extrapolated_salsa2.name: observed breakpoint ratio, applied once more
extrapolated_salsa2.note: Deliberately naive: the measured jump was exactly 4.00x for a step of 8 dimensions, and this applies the same factor to a step of 10 dimensions with a higher h. Included as a transparent lower reference, not as a defensible model.

extrapolated_salsa2.name: power law in n
extrapolated_salsa2.note: Polynomial growth; between linear and exponential.

throughput_basis.source: measured in the completed Salsa 2.0 n=30 pilot

uncertainty: Only TWO positive breakpoints exist. Every two-parameter model fits them exactly, so the fits carry no residual and no goodness-of-fit evidence; model choice, not data, drives the answer.
Both measured breakpoints have h=2, while the target has h=3. Models A, B, D and E cannot see that change and are biased LOW by construction.
Only one n=30 pilot exists, and it produced no breakpoint - a censored observation. It bounds the answer from below (>100,032) and nothing more.
Sample-efficiency scaling need not stay linear, polynomial or exponential across this range; a regime change between n=20 and n=30 would invalidate all five models equally.
Model capacity has not been varied. 4.13M may be adequate at n=12-20 and inadequate at n=30, in which case no sample budget succeeds and the whole extrapolation is moot.
The n=20 run had not converged when its budget ran out - its loss was still falling - so its breakpoint is the earliest detectable one, not the point of useful performance.
The five models span a factor of 29x at n=30. A prediction with that spread cannot be settled by one more training run.
